overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the Feb. 13 meeting was accessible in person and via the Webinar ID on the notice despite an incorrect Zoom link. It declined to review public hearing or city code remote-access questions.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Feb. 13 meeting lacked adequate alternative public access because the Zoom link on the notice was wrong, so the public could not join remotely.
allegations.key_passage: We find here that the February 13 meeting was accessible where an individual could attend the meeting by means of the information posted on the notice, such as through the Webinar ID number and passcode, as the complainant was able to do, and follow the proceedings of the Board in real time.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged that, without working remote access, the complainant could not participate in the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body allow public participation in its meetings

allegations.summary: Concern that lack of remote access prevented public participation in hearings; the AG was asked to assess whether public hearing requirements were met.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to review, and offer no opinion on, whether any actions taken by the Board could be a violation of any public hearing law or regulation.
